title: execution_shortfall.v1
description: One trading session's per-order implementation shortfall against the DECISION price, written by the trader (`nousergon/crucible-trader`) at `crucible.execution.execution_shortfall_key(trading_day)` and reduced by `crucible.report` into the fifth attribution row, `execution_shortfall_bps` (plan §4.5, §9.5; `alpha-engine-config-I10652`). The harness never reaches into the trader: this document is the artifact the trader agreed to write. Cross-field rules JSON Schema cannot state (decided_at <= submitted_at; shortfall_bps re-derivable from side, decision_price and fill_price; the summary equal to the sum of its orders; outcome/orders agreement; the daily metric equal to the summary) are enforced by `crucible.execution.validate_execution_shortfall`, which every consumer calls.

schema_version.description: Version of THIS schema. A consumer that cannot read the version refuses the document rather than guessing.

trading_day.description: The NYSE session the orders were placed in (§4.12). The key.

calendar_date.description: Wall-clock date the document was written. Provenance only, never a key.

champion.description: The arm id whose cross-section the orders were sized from.

decision_price_basis.description: WHICH price shortfall is measured against, recorded rather than implied by code: the price observed at the instant the sizing decision was taken — not the arrival price at submission and not the previous close. A producer measuring against anything else cannot write this document.

shortfall_scope.description: What the bps figure covers: the filled quantity's execution price against the decision price. The opportunity cost of an unfilled remainder (the Perold implementation-shortfall residual) is NOT in the figure; unfilled orders are carried with a null shortfall so the gap is visible rather than averaged away.

outcome.description: `no_orders` is a FACT (the trader placed nothing this session). `not_computed` is a PRODUCER FAILURE (orders were placed and shortfall was not measured) and renders the attribution row RED. The two are never collapsed: an absent row on a traded day is the defect this field exists to name.

outcome_reason.description: Required (non-empty) when outcome is `not_computed` or `no_orders`; null when `computed`.

band.description: The declared band (plan §9.5 paper→live entry condition 2). Lower is better. The row is RED when the window's notional-weighted shortfall, or its CI's upper bound, reaches `upper_bps`.

baseline_bps.description: The fill a perfect execution would get: the decision price itself.

upper_bps.description: The red line. Must exceed baseline_bps.

placeholder.description: True when the band is a declared stand-in rather than a calibrated tolerance. Rendered in the row's reason so a stand-in is never read as a calibration.

summary.description: Null only when outcome is `not_computed`. `notional_usd` is the ABSOLUTE companion to the bps ratio: a ratio cannot catch a book that has collapsed to nothing (measured 2026-09-08, xsec_variance_share).

shortfall_bps_notional_weighted.description: shortfall_usd / decision_notional_usd × 1e4. Null iff nothing filled.

metrics.description: MetricRecord-shaped rows (`crucible.models.MetricRecordRow`). A `computed` document carries exactly one named `execution_shortfall_bps` whose value is the summary's notional-weighted bps.

decided_at_utc.description: The sizing-decision instant the decision price was observed at.

fill_price.description: Volume-weighted fill price; null iff filled_quantity is 0.

shortfall_bps.description: side_sign × (fill_price − decision_price) / decision_price × 1e4; positive is a cost. Null iff unfilled.

decision_notional_usd.description: filled_quantity × decision_price — the weight a notional-weighted shortfall uses, so the weighted figure over identical orders equals each order's own bps.
